title: Fragile struct in6_addr redefinition detection in ipv6_addr.h
description: Location: ipv6_addr.h:43-56. Detection of existing in6_addr relies on checking preprocessor guards: _NETINET_IN_H, _NETINET_IN_H_, _NETINET6_IN6_H, __NETINET_IN_H__, ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_POSIX_NETINET_IN_H_. This list is incomplete (misses musl, bionic, newlib variants) and will break silently if a new libc is used. On redefinition, compiler may error or silently use wrong struct. Consider using __has_include or a configure-time check instead.
close_reason: Dedup: same root cause as 1www.61 and rwio.57. The fragile guard-macro detection list (_NETINET_IN_H, _NETINET_IN_H_, _NETINET6_IN6_H, __NETINET_IN_H__, ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_POSIX_NETINET_IN_H_, _STRUCT_IN6_ADDR) and the IN6ADDR_ANY_INIT heuristic are DELETED in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.h, replaced by the __has_include(<netinet/in.h>) actually-include-it strategy this bead suggested (guard macros can no longer be wrong because the real system header's own include guard does the work; musl/bionic/newlib/BSD covered by construction). LICHEN_HAVE_IN6_ADDR=1 user override retained for exotic toolchains without __has_include. Verified: 4-mode clang -fsyntax-only -Werror matrix incl. -nostdinc bare-metal fallback with _Static_assert(sizeof(struct in6_addr)==16); host pubkey_to_iid cmake test pass; real Zephyr nrf52840dk build of tests/icmpv6 link clean; cppcheck shows no new findings (pre-existing standalone-header unusedStructMember confirmed identical on HEAD).
